Social Organisation & Disorganisation

Social organisation, social control, and social disorganisation such as crime and family breakdown.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Define social organisation and social disorganisation
  • Describe agents of social control
  • Explain how social disorganisation affects health

In simple words

Social organisation is a stable, orderly society where people know their roles and institutions work well. Social disorganisation is the breakdown of that order — when families, communities or institutions fail to support people.

Disorganisation such as crime, family breakdown, unemployment or migration can harm health and make nursing care harder.

Agents of social control

These keep society orderly:

  • Family — teaches norms from childhood.
  • School — teaches rules and roles.
  • Religion — gives moral guidance.
  • Law and police — enforce rules.
  • Media — shows what is accepted.

Social disorganisation

Causes: poverty, unemployment, rapid urbanisation, migration, family breakdown, war, natural disasters.

Effects: crime, substance abuse, neglect of children and elders, poor mental health, less access to care.

Health effects

People in disorganised communities may live in unsafe housing, eat poorly, delay treatment and miss follow-up. Nurses should assess social support and link patients with welfare services.

🔴 Disorganisation harms health

Social disorganisation — poverty, crime, family breakdown — worsens health and delays care. Assess the patient’s social support.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Assess the home situation — ask who lives with the patient and who can help after discharge.
  • Spot neglect — poor hygiene, missed appointments or untreated illness may signal family breakdown.
  • Link to services — tell patients about welfare schemes, shelters and counselling.
  • Protect vulnerable people — children, older adults and people with disability need extra watch.
  • Report abuse — if you suspect abuse, follow hospital policy and inform the right authority.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Social organisation is stable, orderly society with working institutions.
  2. Social disorganisation is the breakdown of social order.
  3. Agents of social control: family, school, religion, law, media.
  4. Causes of disorganisation: poverty, unemployment, migration, family breakdown.
  5. Disorganisation harms health and delays treatment.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Rapid urbanisation can weaken traditional support.
  2. Crime and substance abuse are signs of disorganisation.
  3. Nurses should assess social support and refer to welfare services.

📌 Memory trick

Agents of control: “F-S-R-L-M” — Family, School, Religion, Law, Media.

60-second revision

  • Social organisation = orderly society.
  • Social disorganisation = breakdown of order.
  • Control agents: family, school, religion, law, media.
  • Causes: poverty, unemployment, migration, family breakdown.
  • Effects: crime, neglect, poor mental health, delayed care.
  • Assess support; refer to welfare services.

Test yourself

Social disorganisation is:

Answer: B. Disorganisation is the breakdown of institutions and social order.

Which is an agent of social control?

Answer: B. Family teaches norms and is an agent of social control.

A cause of social disorganisation is:

Answer: B. Unemployment weakens families and communities and can lead to disorganisation.

Disorganisation affects health by:

Answer: B. Disorganised communities face poor housing, bad diet and delayed care.

The nurse should assess:

Answer: B. Assessing social support helps plan discharge and follow-up care.
